text: Bath shall hold a heated vessel at a set temperature, with one arbiter as the only writer to the heater, and the same code shall run in simulation and against the wall clock.
acceptance: All children verified.
rationale: This merges Modulo's Bath and Morphyx's Keyholder (council 2) into one plant, one harness, one log and one latch.

text: The controller shall raise a safety demand toward heater off on every condition it cannot trust.
acceptance: All children verified.
rationale: Modulo: a controller that is wrong and off costs a batch, and one that is wrong and on costs a kitchen. In the merge the controller detects the fault and the arbiter latches.

text: A safety demand shall be raised, and the heater shall be off, within 5 s of sim time after the last sensor reading.
acceptance: T-SAFE-STALE passes: with the sensor silenced at 10800 s and a boost held on at 10800 s, the heater is off by 10805 s under both control laws.
rationale: Modulo's leaf. The only change is the boost: Morphyx measured a second writer defeating this fail-safe in 76.5% and 80.5% of trials.

text: A reading more than 5 K above the set point shall raise a safety demand at that step.
acceptance: T-SAFE-OVER passes: a reading of set+5.1 K gives heater off at that step, and a reading of set+5.0 K raises no demand.
rationale: This is Modulo's over-temperature latch with the latching moved to the arbiter. As written, Bath and Keyholder each hold a latch. Built together, a reset that clears one would leave the other holding the heater off, silently, so there is one latch and it lives in the arbiter.

text: The test suite shall fail when the controller reaches the set point in simulation in less than 50 percent of the readings it was sent.
acceptance: T-SAFE-STARVE passes: a controller ticking at the sensor period is detected as starved (fixture: max 20.29 C after 4 h).
rationale: Modulo measured this: des signals aren't buffered, so a 1 s tick racing a 1 s sensor drops readings, and the fail-safe then holds the heater off for good.

text: A reading that is non-finite or outside -10..105 C shall raise a safety demand at that step, and heating that produces less than a third of the rise the plant model predicts over 160 s shall raise a safety demand.
acceptance: T-SAFE-PLAUSIBLE passes: -127, NaN and a reading frozen at 59.0, each injected at 10800 s under both laws, keep the plant under set + 5 K; no seed 1-20 healthy run trips it, on the modelled plant and on plants differing from the check model by the fit error bounds and at least heater -20%, dead time x3, room -8 K (proposals/morphyx-mismatch.mjs). The no-rise clause reads its parameters from the table with provenance (assumed or a fit id), runs on hardware only on fitted parameters, and logs a trip as "heating disagrees with model <id>". The no-rise clause is not verified before fit.mjs exists.
rationale: Modulo measured it: stale and over-temperature trust the value, and -127, NaN or a frozen reading boil the pot in 6 of 8 cases with all other leaves passing. Morphyx measured the mismatch: on its own model the check is clean, off it it trips 7-20 of 20 healthy runs, so it judges the model as much as the sensor. Folded in by Mozzie, round 2.

text: Authority over the heater shall be data that a person can read, not an order of calls in code.
acceptance: All children verified.
rationale: Morphyx: a rule nobody wrote down is just whoever's code ran last.

text: The arbiter shall be the only code path that calls the heater driver.
acceptance: T-TABLE-ONLY passes: (a) a source scan finds no driver call outside keyholder.mjs, and (b) a driver called without the arbiter's private token throws.
rationale: Morphyx's sketch: one extra direct writer ran the heater on a dead sensor in 76.5% and 80.5% of trials.

text: The arbiter shall refuse to start with a table that names an unknown source or actuator, lacks a safe state for an actuator, or ranks any non-safety source above a safety source.
acceptance: T-TABLE-REJECT passes: each of 4 malformed fixture tables throws at construction and names the offending entry, and the shipped table loads.
rationale: Morphyx's leaf, with one shipped table instead of two. The gate is deferred (see the proposal).

text: A safety demand shall outrank every other source.
acceptance: All children verified.
rationale: Morphyx's reason: Therac-25.

text: While a safety latch is held, the arbiter shall keep the heater off whatever other sources command.
acceptance: T-SAFE-OUTRANK passes: over 1000 seeded random command sequences, there are zero instants where the latch is held and the heater is on.
rationale: Morphyx's sketch: 0 of 400 trials, against 314 of 400 under last-writer-wins.

text: The arbiter shall apply a safety demand at the sim instant the demand is raised.
acceptance: T-SAFE-PROMPT passes: a latch raised at t while another source holds the heater on gives heater off at t, without any other source asking.
rationale: Morphyx's first draft waited for the next request, and a boost already running kept heating a dead bath in 3-4% of trials.

text: A latch shall be lifted only by an operator reset received while every permissive the table names holds.
acceptance: T-SAFE-RESET passes: a reset with a stale reading, or with a reading above set+5 K, is refused and logged with the failing permissive. A reset with fresh, in-range readings lifts the latch. No other source lifts it.
rationale: This merges Modulo's 'off until an operator reset' with Morphyx's permissives, so stale-sensor and over-temperature faults share one reset path.

text: The suite shall run the last-writer-wins arrangement as a negative control and shall fail it.
acceptance: T-NEG-LWW passes: the T-SAFE-OUTRANK property, run against last-writer-wins, finds a violation within 1000 sequences.
rationale: This is Morphyx's KEY-PLANT-NEG, moved under KEY-SAFE because it guards the outrank test, not a plant.

text: The controller shall regulate temperature within stated limits on the plant model.
acceptance: All children verified.
rationale: Modulo: the control law is the part that can be tuned offline.

text: From 30 min after first reaching set minus 0.5 K, the 1st to 99th percentile of plant temperature shall lie within set plus or minus 1 K, over seeds 1 to 20.
acceptance: T-CTL-BAND passes on all 20 seeds, with the arbiter in the loop.
rationale: Modulo's sizing on the assumed plant: bang-bang -0.56..+0.93 K, PI -0.08..+0.18 K.

text: Overshoot on the first approach shall not exceed 1.5 K over seeds 1 to 20.
acceptance: T-CTL-OVER passes on all 20 seeds, with the arbiter in the loop.
rationale: Modulo's sizing: bang-bang 1.01-1.06 K, PI 0.22-0.23 K.

text: Heater switch commands per hour, counted at the driver, shall not exceed the rated limit of the switching device named in the configuration.
acceptance: T-CTL-WEAR passes for a limit of 60 per hour (mechanical relay) and 3600 per hour (solid-state relay), each with the law the configuration selects, counting switches from every source.
rationale: Modulo's leaf. Counting happens at the driver because the boost button switches the relay too, and the relay doesn't care who asked.

text: Every decision the arbiter makes shall be logged with its reason and shall replay.
acceptance: All children verified.
rationale: Morphyx: an operator who can read a refusal has a rule they can argue with.

text: Each heater change and each refused command shall produce one log entry naming the source, the command, and the table rule that decided it.
acceptance: T-LOG-REASON passes: in 20 seeded runs, heater changes match change entries one for one, and every refusal names a rule id present in the table.
rationale: Morphyx's leaf, unchanged.

text: A decision log from a fake-clock realtime run shall replay under run() to identical decisions.
acceptance: T-LOG-REPLAY passes on a 600 s fake-clock run with 600 readings, a dropout, a boost and a reset, and fails when one logged reading is altered.
rationale: Modulo's BATH-RT-REPLAY and Morphyx's KEY-LOG-REPLAY were the same leaf, so it's kept once with both acceptances. Mozzie's sizing: a day at 1 reading/s is 3 MB and replays from t=0 in about 50 ms here, so no checkpoint leaf is needed yet.

text: The plant model shall be fitted to the real vessel before any control-law limit is trusted.
acceptance: All children verified.
rationale: Modulo: every plant number is assumed.

text: A fit tool shall recover heat capacity, loss coefficient, dead time and ambient offset from a logged open-loop response to a stated input shape, and shall not recommend a test input that exceeds the vessel's limit.
acceptance: T-PLANT-FIT passes: on logs from 3 known plants with 0.05 K sensor noise, 0.0625 K quantization and ambient misstated by up to 0.5 K, heat capacity and loss coefficient are within 5 percent and dead time within 10 s, for the input: 5 min baseline, full on until 30 K below boiling or the vessel limit, then off with logging for 1 h. The recommended input's simulated peak stays under the limit.
rationale: Modulo's leaf, amended in council 2 round 1 on his measurement (modulo-fit.mjs, reproduced by Mozzie). With ambient known the fit is nearly circular, within 0.1 percent at 1 h for every input shape. With ambient 0.5 K wrong, dead time is off by up to 36 s. My original ask, flat out for N hours, peaks at 113.2 C. So ambient is fitted, the input is bounded, and step length stops being the question.

text: The fitted model shall predict a second, held-out step response of the real vessel with RMS error under 0.5 K.
acceptance: A-PLANT-REAL: fit on step 1, predict step 2, RMS under 0.5 K. Unverified until a vessel exists.
rationale: Modulo: this is the only leaf that says the simulation is about the real thing.

text: The installed controller shall be shown safe and timely on the machine it runs on.
acceptance: All children verified.
rationale: These are the two leaves nobody can verify from this lab. They're reported as unverified, not rounded up.

text: On the target machine, 99th percentile lateness of controller steps against the wall clock shall be under 50 ms.
acceptance: D-RT-LATE: 2000 steps of 10 ms on the target, with lateness measured from before runRealtime is called, p99 under 50 ms.
rationale: Modulo measured p99 at 1.6-2.1 ms on the lab machine, which isn't the target.

text: The installed machine shall have a cutout that no software path can command.
acceptance: The person records, with a photograph of the wiring, a thermal fuse or bimetal cutout in series with the element, outside the computer's reach.
rationale: Both proposals say this in nearly the same words: a fuse doesn't run JavaScript.
